$$

question.knowledge_point: Finding Differences of Sets Given Verbally
question.problem: Let $A$  be the set of all multiples of $3$ greater than $0$ and let $B$  be the set of all multiples of $4$ greater than $0.$ What is $B-A?$
question.worked_solution:
The multiples of $3$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
A=\{3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24,…\}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
B=\{4,8,12,16,20,24,…\}.
$$

Now, $B-A$ is the *difference* of $B$ and $A,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $B$ but *not* in $A.$

The elements of $B$ that are also in $A$ are $12,24,$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $12$). So, we must remove these elements from $B.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B-A & =\{4,8,12,16,20,24,…\}-\{3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24,…\} \\  & =\{4,8,16,20,…\}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
C=\{10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…\}.

$$

$$

question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 & 6 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 & 6 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Reducing a 2x2 Augmented Matrix to REF Using Gaussian Elimination
question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & 11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-1\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x+y=8 \\  & y=-11,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-11$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+(-11)=8\,⇒\,x=8+11=19.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=19$ and $y=-11.$

question.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
question.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & 2x-4y=6 \\  & 4x-7y=10.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 6 \\ 4 & -7 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 6 \\ 4 & -7 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & -7 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x-2y=3 \\  & y=-2,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-2$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(-2)=3\,⇒\,x=-1.
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-1$ and $y=-2.$

question.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & 3x-2y=4 \\  & 2x-y=2.\end{aligned}

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Writing a Function Using Arrow Notation
question.problem:
Which of the following is the correct symbolic notation for the sentence given below?

*"The function $f$ maps the set of real numbers to the set $Y.$"*
question.worked_solution:
The sentence *"The function $f$ maps the set of real numbers to the set $Y$"* is equivalent to the following symbolic notation:

$\,$ $f:R\to Y$

Here, the domain of $f$ is $R,$ and the codomain of $f$ is $Y.$

question.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $g(x)=x-3{x}^{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
The notation $g(x)=x-3{x}^{2}$ means that the function $g$ maps the element $x$ in the domain to $x-3{x}^{2}$ in the codomain. This can also be written as

$$
g:x↦x-3{x}^{2}.
$$

question.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination
question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 5 & 0 & 6 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
question.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 5 & 0 & 6 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination
question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 & -6 \\ 2 & 7 & 9 & -13 \\ 4 & 12 & 17 & -26\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
question.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 & -6 \\ 2 & 7 & 9 & -13 \\ 4 & 12 & 17 & -26\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 4 & 12 & 17 & -26\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
